Give a reason. Include up to three complete alternative proposals when another scientific aim is plausible. Mark uncertain and ask one short question only when the scientific aim is ambiguous; the recorded recommendation is used in the autonomous arm. Never invent columns or outcomes. Per-column values/counts and numeric summaries are provided; no raw rows or researcher manifest. An optional label_map maps target-column names to observed spelling replacements, with label_map_reason. Both source and destination labels must occur in the column; only whitespace, case or trailing-period variants of the same label may merge. Never merge distinct outcomes. [RL-0002] Choose problem_type from the schema. Two observed values in the outcome: binary. Three or more discrete labels: multiclass. Several categorical outcome columns describing the same row at different levels of detail: multilabel, with all of them as targets. One numeric measurement or count: regression. Two or more numeric outcomes recorded together: multioutput_regression. If no column is a plausible outcome, choose clustering when rows are entities or events to segment, and representation when the table is many homogeneous numeric features of one kind. Prefer the task the table was evidently assembled for over an incidental column.
[RL-0003] List as leakage_suspects every column that is a component, sum, difference, rescaling or recoding of a target, or that is known only after the outcome (for example the raw score a binary target was derived from, or partial counts that add up to a total). List as identifier_suspects row keys, record numbers and codes with nearly one unique value per row. Never propose either kind as a feature.
[RL-0004] Set group_column when a non-target column repeats across rows and identifies the source unit (subject, recording, customer, device), so its rows must stay in one partition. List time_columns when rows are consecutive periods of one series, regardless of the stated prediction aim, or when the aim is to predict later periods. Use columns that establish chronological order, not redundant seasonal encodings. Leave both empty when no such column exists; do not invent them. Declare constraints for the final analysis units, not merely every raw event field. When clustering or segmenting static entities from transactional records, leave time_columns empty; transaction timestamps used only to aggregate static features (such as recency relative to an observation date) are not time columns for partitioning. Consecutive periods of a single series still require chronology.
